claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished in the fourth and fifth centuries, with approximate dates of 355 to 408/425.
Severian was a popular preacher in Constantinople from around 400 until 404.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Severian was Syrian by birth and spoke Greek with a Syriac accent.
Severian came to Constantinople about 400, provided with a series of Greek sermons.
John Chrysostom appointed Severian his representative for liturgical functions when Chrysostom went to Asia in 401.
Severian was opposed and insulted by the deacon Sarapion, to whom Chrysostom had delegated the Church's economic affairs, leading to enmity between Severian and Chrysostom.
Severian was regarded by his contemporaries as a good preacher and was known as the author of Biblical commentaries and sermons.
A manuscript in the Vatican Library (Vat. gr. 2217) contains a fragment of Severian's commentary on 1 Corinthians 6:18, edited by K. Staab in 1933.
Almost all of Severian's homilies survive in Greek only among the works of his enemy Chrysostom.
SCOPE: this English is In epistulam i ad Corinthios, the fragments stored for severianus-in-1cor. His sermons are a different body of work.
